Thought: I need to identify the functional groups in oxybenzone. Oxybenzone (benzophenone-3) is a common UV filter used in sunscreens. From my knowledge of organic chemistry, oxybenzone has the following structure:

It contains:
- A ketone group (C=O) connecting two benzene rings
- An ether group (-O-) as a substituent on one of the benzene rings
- A phenol group (aromatic ring with -OH) on the same benzene ring as the ether

Looking at the options:
A. Aldehyde and ether - Oxybenzone has an ether but no aldehyde
B. Ester, phenol and carboxylic acid - Oxybenzone has a phenol but no ester or carboxylic acid
C. Ketone and carboxylic acid - Oxybenzone has a ketone but no carboxylic acid
D. Ketone, ether and phenol - Oxybenzone has all three: ketone, ether, and phenol
Final Answer: [ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
